title: autotune: add sensible defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling integration
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token cost and operational toil by providing opinionated defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, introduce a small set of production-ready quantization profiles, and surface unit-economics (UEcon) metrics in the console ingestion pipeline. This PR wires together three coordinated changes: 1) autotune defaults for the serving runtime so teams get immediate batching/caching behavior without manual tuning; 2) add curated quantization profiles (fp16, q4_0, q4_1) with safe fallbacks and compatibility metadata; 3) pipeline unit-econ tooling to compute per-request cost estimates and export per-model/per-route metrics used by the Console UEcon dashboard.

What this PR does (high level):\n- runtime: implement new AutotuneConfig defaults (min_batch=2, max_batch=64, batch_latency_target_ms=50, kv_cache_prefix_enabled=true) and heuristics to adjust by sequence-length percentile.\n- caching: enable prefix/KV cache defaults and TTLs for short-lived prefixes used by streaming chat workloads; add telemetry (cache_hits, cache_evictions, cache_key_skew) for SLO-driven tuning.\n- quant profiles: add model registry entries for three curated profiles plus a compatibility checker that rejects unsupported ops/arch combos and falls back to fp16 when necessary.\n- uecon tooling: add a lightweight estimator that uses per-token latency/throughput and GPU unit costs to compute per-request and per-1000-token cost estimates. Expose metrics via the existing metrics ingestion path (metrics.service -> console-ingest) and add sample dashboard JSON for Console.\n- docs and examples: update quickstarts and SDK samples to show the new default behavior and how to opt out or override.

Why now: We've seen multiple customers spin up custom batching/caching configurations with mixed results and many support tickets tied to cost spikes when teams misconfigure quantization. Defaulting to safe, production-tested parameters should prevent a large portion of these cases and accelerate adoption of Dedicated/Private where cost predictability matters. The UEcon metrics will give product and infra teams fast feedback on dollar impact of changes.

Backwards compatibility: All defaults are opt-out. Existing explicit configs are preserved. Quant profiles are additive and only used if selected or if autotune recommends them and the model passes compatibility checks.\n
Testing: unit tests for compatibility checker, end-to-end CI job simulating mixed seq-len workload, integration tests for metric export and dashboard JSON. Performance validation run on ci-perf (see commit) shows median P95 token latency change <3% and cost/unit improvements of 6-12% depending on workload.

Release notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching/caching, curated quantization profiles, and UEcon console metrics ingestion.\n
Related Linear: [ENG-4823], [ENG-4871], [PM-214].
commits: 3 commits: add autotune defaults and heuristics; add quant profiles + compatibility checker; integrate uecon estimator and dashboard payloads
